done_when: Each task and fix keeps one worker chat per tool from its first round to merge: a later round resumes it even after a model or effort change, a Forge or machine restart, or a fresh worktree of the same item; a fresh chat starts only when the recorded chat truly can't be resumed (the tool reports it gone, or the item moved to the other tool), and then the round says why in one line; plan reads keep their reader chat across rounds the same way; the coordinator guide says so; command tests with stubbed Codex and Claude cover each resume case and each fresh-chat reason, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Not done — a later round can resume an obsolete worker or reader chat and overwrite the current binding. At line 196, local JSON takes precedence over the committed state or read notes. In a normal two-machine flow, machine B may be told that machine A’s chat is gone, start a replacement, and commit its ID. When A updates the branch, its older local JSON still wins. The next round resumes the old ID; a worker round can also commit that ID back over the replacement through `remember()`.
findings.title: Not done: A stale local record can replace the current chat

findings.body: Raise: Not done — an unmerged spec reader loses its chat after upgrade when that spec also exists on the default branch. If its old owning worktree was removed, line 245 selects the upgrade checkout as owner merely because it contains the spec, before searching the retained work branch. Sync then writes or skips the binding there, leaving the unmerged branch without its reader ID. Recreating that branch after local metadata loss starts a fresh chat. The named moved-owner tests explicitly use a spec absent from the default checkout, so they do not cover this common amendment flow.
findings.title: Not done: Upgrade can bind a spec reader to the wrong branch

stop.reason: Owner wants every in-flight fix finished; narrowed to the two remaining findings: Codex's real missing-rollout wording, and reader chats archived by an earlier release

why: Worker chats should be reused: each task or fix should keep the same worker conversation from its first round until it merges, but today some rounds start a fresh chat (for example when the model or effort changes, after Forge restarts, or when a record is missing), losing context and costing tokens (owner, 2026-10-09)
